summary.headline: Finolex Industries Q2 FY27 volume rose 28% YoY to 83,407 MT, but PBT was flat at INR153 crore as raw material cost lag squeezed margins.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 sales volume grew 28% YoY to 83,407 MT as channel restocking followed Q1 price-led destocking, and revenue rose 27% to INR1,094 crore. PBT was roughly flat at INR153 crore versus INR158 crore a year earlier, as higher-cost inventory consumed in Q2 lagged the rise in PVC prices. H1 volume fell 4% YoY to 151,106 MT and H1 revenue rose 4% to INR1,978 crore. Management guided full-year EBITDA of about INR15/kg (roughly 14-15%) and said October was a good month.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR158 crore in Q2 FY26 (flat to down)
vs 157,465 MT in H1 FY26 (-4% YoY)
Management said H1 EBITDA margin in line with last year

financial_highlights.metric: Net free cash flow / cash position
financial_highlights.value: About INR2,584 crore as of 30 Sep 2026

segments.name: Pipes and fittings
segments.commentary: Overall utilisation about 68% in Q2; agri to non-agri mix about 60:40 in Q2 versus 56:44 in Q2 FY26. Fittings were about 12% of Q2 local volume and CPVC about 8%.

segments.name: Resin (EDC/VCM)
segments.commentary: EDC line runs at full utilisation; VCM line is structurally idle during monsoon due to raw material unavailability. Q2 PVC-EDC spread was USD455/t and PVC-VCM spread USD171/t (ICIS SE Asia).

guidance_outlook: Full-year EBITDA guided at roughly INR15/kg on average, or about 14-15% margin; management said H1 was about 12.5% and full year about 12.5-13% to 14%, a range it hedged.
No large PVC price erosion expected in Q3 as the minimum import price remains until mid to third week of January and domestic supply-demand is slightly constrained.
Management said October was relatively good and volume was slightly positive YoY for the period to date, but it did not want to raise expectations.
Capex of about INR150 crore planned for FY27, mainly debottlenecking and routine maintenance; new capacity expected only towards end of FY28.
Raw materials covered for Q3; management said procurement cost is in line with existing inventory cost, not below spot.
capex_capacity: Total pipe and fitting capacity stated at 520,000 MT, with fittings about 95,000 MT of which about 40,000 MT in-house and about 60,000 MT outsourced.
Utilisation about 68% in Q2; management said there is sufficient headroom for the current and next year without new capacity.
Debottlenecking replaces low-capacity extruders with higher-capacity ones; incremental capacity expected towards end of FY28.
Monetisation of idle plant was completed about two years ago; no current plan to monetise further land at Ratnagiri, Masar or Urse.
demand_pricing: Q2 volume recovery was driven by channel restocking after Q1 price-led destocking; PVC prices stabilised in Q2 with lower volatility.
Agri demand is at risk from El Nino and water scarcity, but management cited tractor bookings up 14-15% and rural 2-wheeler bookings above prior years.
Management said scheme and discount spend offset PVC price increases, flattening realisations despite higher PVC prices.
Q2 margin pressure attributed to a lag in raw material cost: inventory bought at lower prices in Q1 was consumed in Q2 while selling prices reset immediately.

Spot prices: EDC USD450-500/t, VCM USD900-950/t, ethylene USD1,150-1,200/t. The MIP on suspension-grade PVC resin is USD767/t CIF; DGTR has recommended CVD on PVC from China, with the Ministry of Finance yet to decide and the CVD likely to replace the MIP if adopted.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins under pressure despite higher raw material prices and possible inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1-bought low-cost inventory was consumed in Q2 while realisations fall immediately, so the raw-material lag squeezed margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is full-year volume and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year EBITDA about INR15/kg, roughly 14-15%; October was a relatively good month and volume was slightly positive YoY to date, but management avoided firm guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growth equal to volume growth despite higher PVC prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited product mix (agri growing faster than non-agri, 60:40 vs 56:44) and higher channel schemes and discounts.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and capital allocation of the large cash pile?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR150 crore planned for FY27; Board has made no decision on use or reward for cash, which stays invested at about 7.5-8% yield, with no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for agri demand given El Nino?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said El Nino impact expected from November; water-led pipe demand may rise but farmer income may be constrained, offset by strong tractor and rural two-wheeler bookings.

qa_highlights.question: Supply chain impact from Middle East disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the disruption affected crude and petrochemical supply chains, but teams re-established supply from other sources; EDC and VCM are 100% imported.

risks_watch: Geopolitical disruption in West Asia affecting crude, petrochemical and shipping costs and PVC/EDC/VCM supply.
El Nino and water scarcity weighing on agri demand, which is about 60% of volume in Q2.
Margin sustainability: EBITDA/kg target depends on resin price and inventory costing; any price drop after the MIP ends in January could hit margins.
Trade policy: MIP status and DGTR-recommended CVD on Chinese PVC pending Ministry of Finance decision.
Capital allocation: about INR2,584 crore cash with no Board decision on use or shareholder reward; an analyst pressed for a timeline.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management was confident on volume recovery and Q3 pricing, but evasive on full-year volume, margin ranges, and the timing of cash deployment.
key_quotes: So what is also is that the second half of this year looks like January to May, which is the pre-monsoon window, which is seasonally our strongest period in terms of our volumes.
So on a full year basis, we are expecting EBITDA margin roughly around INR15 per kg on an average.
No. Certainly, the Board has to take a call on this.
Right now, there is no such decision. This -- whatever we have continues to remain invested into different instruments.

adds.what: Debottlenecking replacing low-capacity extruders with higher-capacity ones (no new plant); incremental capacity expected towards end of FY28

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14-15% (INR14-15/kg) and FY27 capex of about INR150 crore, mainly debottlenecking, with new capacity only toward end-FY28; H1 revenue is guided up only ~4% YoY on volume down 4%, so revenue growth guidance is not explicitly stated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA about INR15/kg (roughly 14-15%) versus H1 about 12.5%, implying a H2 step-up, but the range is hedged and the Q2 raw-material lag squeezed margins while PVC prices may ease after the MIP ends in mid-January.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is about 68% against 520,000 MT capacity with headroom for the current and next year; only debottlenecking (INR150 crore FY27 capex) is planned, with incremental capacity only towards end of FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume rose 28% YoY to 83,407 MT on channel restocking, October was slightly positive YoY, and tractor bookings are up 14-15%, but H1 volume is still down 4% YoY to 151,106 MT and El Nino threatens agri demand (about 60% of volume).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 68%, the Board has no plan to monetise further land, and capex of about INR150 crore for FY27 is debottlenecking and maintenance, so a new large capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 EBITDA of 14-15% and avoided firm volume guidance, saying it did not want to raise expectations despite a good October.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin was about 12.5% and the full-year range was hedged at 12.5-13% to 14%; a PVC price drop after the January MIP expiry could hit margins, and El Nino could hit agri demand.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launches were discussed; the call covered only fittings and CPVC mix at existing lines.

rows.label: PVC price path after MIP expiry and possible CVD on Chinese PVC
rows.why: No large PVC price erosion is expected in Q3 while the MIP (USD767/t CIF) stays until mid-to-third week of January, but DGTR has recommended a CVD on Chinese PVC that the Ministry of Finance has yet to decide, and that would replace the MIP.

rows.label: Raw material cost lag reversing in H2
rows.why: Raw materials are covered for Q3 at roughly existing inventory cost, which management said is not below spot, so the Q2 lag from low-cost Q1 inventory should not repeat in Q3 at the same scale.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume recovery and Q3 pricing but cautious and evasive on full-year volume, the hedged margin range and timing of cash deployment; analysts pressed on the margin lag, the capital allocation timeline and El Nino risk to agri demand.
